title: Brief provider — a feed-forward brief of guarantees and their state, pushed into the phase's first prompt and pulled with `phax brief`

ground.note: The author's decisions of 2026-10-05/06. The need by moment: before writing and while writing. Where the phase stands is the gate commands' job, not the brief's. The answer carries state, not only the rule. One provider and one request serve two verbs (`steme brief`, `steme audit`). `phax brief` runs with or without a path. A brief never blocks. The spec is purely additive after `drop-orient`. The hello-world example gains a brief provider, and steme is the first provider. Provider answers carry `$schema` too (2026-10-06). §9 Q1–Q6 were decided on 2026-10-05 and Q7–Q9 on 2026-10-06.

Approved earlier on 2026-10-06, then abandoned only to add the answer-`$schema` rule. Its design, surface and §9 Q1–Q9 carry over unchanged. This spec adds Q10 and the requirements, surface and criteria that follow from it.

Abandoned 2026-10-06. Its context, surface and §9 are the ground for this design, minus the retirement of orient, which `drop-orient` now owns. It used exit 2 for `phax brief` usage errors, which README §Exit codes reserves for plan or config validation.

Approved. The gate request is `{$schema, phase, base, terminal, phases}`. `base` is the commit the phase branch was created from. phax notes it when it creates the branch, so it is stable across attempts, resumes, resets and appends. `phases` is `[{id, files}]` (create ∪ edit, optional files excluded), every phase of the run in execution order. Only steps declaring `"input": "gate-request"` receive it, and a copy `checks-attempt-NN.request.json` is saved beside each attempt. A diagnostics step already prints `{"$schema": "…/gate-diagnostics/<release>.json", "diagnostics": [...]}`.

Every finding a diagnostics step reports fails the step, so the audit alone decides what is due. A finding's location is `{file, line?}`. The diagnostics document a step prints requires `$schema`. phax decodes every release it supports through the schemas package's history mechanism and refuses a newer one by name. A document with no `$schema` fails, with no fallback. The hello-world example loses `scopes.mjs`. The re-authored spec was not under docs/specs/ in this session, so it was read from its brief.

Removed with no shim: orient, `phax orient`, its prompt section, `orient-brief.json`, the `orient` grant source and its telemetry. The `security.json` grant source becomes `config | gate`. A leftover `orient` key is an ordinary unknown key.

The history mechanism every persisted format uses. A `$schema` URL resolves to the latest release-named shape at or below its release. A newer release fails at `$schema` and names the format and release. Another format's URL fails, and so does a release with no known shape. A format born with `$schema` (`preSchema: null`) fails when the key is missing, and no decoder is tried.

The contract every extension point shares. The command is split on whitespace and run with no shell. JSON goes on stdin, and phax expects exit 0 with JSON on stdout. Failures are typed: exit code, stderr excerpt, invalid JSON, schema failure. An optional `timeoutMs` exists.
A fresh phase start sets up the branch and worktree, then builds the first prompt. A resume reuses both and builds no prompt. As drop-orient leaves it, nothing is queried at phase start.

The first prompt runs: plan, previous handoff, reconciliation, `## Current phase`, `## Execution rules` (which ends with the gate commands the agent may run itself), `## Required output`. As drop-orient leaves it, nothing sits between `## Current phase` and `## Execution rules`.
Nothing ties a worktree back to its run. Each worktree has a gitignored `.phax-context/` folder (PHAX_CONTEXT_DIR), written by the agent (handoff, summary) and by phax.
Provider keys such as `planAuditor` are `{command}`, read from phax.local.json, then ~/.phax/config.json, then phax.json.
A granted agent command records `source`. After drop-orient the values are `config | gate`. `security.json` is phax-internal, not a `@lbdremy/phax-schemas` format.
`phax records explain` has the flags `--prompt`, `--diff`, `--transcript` and `--gates`. Every file in the phase folder goes into the phase record.

§Extend phax counts the hooks. §Persisted formats has the format table. §Exit codes: 1 is generic failure (refusal, bad arguments) and 2 is plan or config validation. Headless authoring uses `phax artifact new spec|plan … --headless --brief <file|->`.
phax.json plus one small script per hook (`audit.mjs`, `audit-plan.mjs`). tests/integration/exampleProviders.test.ts runs them.

§Before steme's audit: drop-orient, drop-gate-scopes, gate-request, then the brief. The plan auditor's answer gets `$schema` in a separate small spec. §Road to 1.0.0: the CLI and config contract freeze.

context:
When `drop-orient` and `drop-gate-scopes` have landed, nothing tells a phase agent about the project's standard before the gate judges its work. The first prompt holds the plan, the previous handoff, the current phase and the execution rules. The rules end with the gate commands, which the agent may run itself to check its work. Every extension point shares one contract. It is a command in `phax.json`, split on whitespace and run without a shell. It reads a JSON request on stdin and prints a JSON answer on stdout. Failures are typed, and there is an optional wall-clock limit. A provider key such as `planAuditor` is `{command}`, read from phax.local.json, then ~/.phax/config.json, then phax.json.

Spec `gate-request` (Approved) lets a gate step declare `"input": "gate-request"` and read the phase facts on stdin:
- `phase`.
- `base`: the commit the phase branch was created from, stable across attempts, resumes, resets and appends.
- `terminal`.
- `phases`: the plan projection `[{id, files}]`.

phax saves a copy beside each attempt. Under `drop-gate-scopes`, every finding a diagnostics step reports fails the step, so the audit alone decides what is due. Every document that crosses a provider boundary is versioned in both directions, which lets phax support several versions. The gate request carries `$schema`, and so does the diagnostics document a step prints (`gate-diagnostics`). phax decodes each through the schemas package's history mechanism: a release it knows decodes with that release's shape, a newer one is refused by name, and a missing `$schema` fails with no fallback.

The retired orient provider shows what a brief must not be. Asked about a list of file names, it answered with rows `{id, title, severity, trigger}`, and on expand with a body: the rule in general, never how the code stands. Its answer was unversioned. It received no phase, no base and no plan. A pull from inside the worktree carried nothing of the phase, pulls were not recorded, and the query at phase start had no time limit.

The agent works inside the phase worktree, and nothing ties that worktree back to its run. Each worktree has a gitignored `.phax-context/` folder, written by the agent (handoff, summary) and by phax. In `secure` mode the agent may run only the commands that `security.json` grants, with source `config` or `gate`.

The first provider is steme. It plans `steme brief` (roadmap-1.0 item 8, not built), which will read the ledger that `steme audit` builds (item 0.13). The word "brief" already names the prose a person gives a headless authoring session (`--brief <file|->`, kept under `docs/briefs/`). NEXT_STEPS §Road to 1.0.0 freezes the CLI and config contract, and this spec adds surface on purpose before that freeze.

productGoal.guidingRule: A brief informs and the audit decides: phax carries the phase's facts to the provider and its versioned answer to the agent, and judges, ranks and filters nothing in between.

terminology.definition: The brief provider's answer about a set of paths: the guarantees that range over them, and the state of each guarantee at each place. It feeds forward and only informs. It never fails, blocks or retries anything.
The gate's diagnostics step (for steme, `steme audit` declaring `"input": "gate-request"`). It blocks: its findings fail the gate. This spec does not change it.
The command configured under `brief`. It reads a brief request on stdin and prints a brief answer on stdout.
The phase's brief. phax requests it once, when a phase starts fresh, and weaves its compact form into the phase's first prompt.
A brief the agent asks for with `phax brief`. phax prints it in whole form.
The keys `phase`, `base`, `terminal` and `phases`, with the values and meanings that the gate request of the same phase carries (spec `gate-request`).

The JSON document on the provider's stdin, in the persisted format `brief-request`. Inside a phase it holds `$schema`, the phase facts and `files`. Outside a phase it holds `$schema` and `files` only.

The JSON document the provider prints on stdout, in the persisted format `brief-answer`: `{$schema, guarantees}`. Its `$schema` is `https://docs.phax.run/schemas/brief-answer/<release>.json` and names the phax release whose answer shape the provider wrote.
A `brief-answer` release no newer than the running phax and no older than the format's first release. phax decodes it with that release's shape.
`.phax-context/brief-request.json` in a phase worktree, written by phax. It holds the phase's brief request with `files: null`. `phax brief` reads it to learn which phase it runs in.

Inside a phase, the top directory of the phase worktree. Outside a phase, the top of the git working tree that contains the current directory. Paths in `files` are relative to it, and the provider runs from it.
One expectation of the project's standard, as the provider knows it: an `id` and a `statement`, with the places it ranges over.
A location `{file, line?}` where a guarantee ranges, with the guarantee's state there. A file that does not exist yet can be a place.

One of four values:
- `met`: the guarantee holds there.
- `missing`: something the guarantee requires is absent.
- `forbidden`: something the guarantee forbids is present.
- `accepted`: a known violation recorded as accepted debt, to leave alone.
The provider's word on when a `missing` or `forbidden` place must be resolved: `this-phase`, `later`, or `null` when the request carried no phase facts. phax never computes or checks it.
One line per guarantee: its id and statement, then the state, location and due of each place that is not `met`. It omits `what` and repair.
Every guarantee with its id and statement. Every place with its state and location, plus its due, `what` and repair wherever the state has them.
A fixed wall-clock limit of 60 seconds on one brief call (Q9). When it passes, phax stops the provider and treats the brief as failed.

A file `brief-NN.json` in the phase folder, in the persisted format `brief-record`. It holds one brief call: its moment, its request as sent, and its outcome. An answered outcome holds the answer as printed. `00` is the pushed brief, and pulled briefs are numbered from `01` in call order.

The prose a person writes for a headless authoring session (`--brief <file|->`, kept under `docs/briefs/`). It shares one sense with the provider brief: what an agent is given before it writes. A person writes the authoring brief for an authoring agent. The brief provider computes a provider brief for a phase agent. The two share no command, key, file or format. Bringing the provider's brief to the authoring moment (the brief at plan authoring) is a later spec.

requirements.title: The `brief` provider key
requirements.statement: WHERE `"brief": { "command": … }` is declared in `phax.json`, `phax.local.json` or `~/.phax/config.json` THE system SHALL use that command as the brief provider, a nearer layer overriding a farther one in the order phax.local.json, then ~/.phax/config.json, then phax.json.

requirements.title: How the provider is run
requirements.statement: The system shall run the brief provider split on whitespace with no shell, from the working tree root of the call.

requirements.title: One request on stdin
requirements.statement: The system shall write exactly one brief request to the brief provider's stdin and then close stdin, for every brief it requests.

requirements.title: The local schemas describe `brief`
requirements.statement: WHEN `phax schema upgrade` runs THE system SHALL write a `phax.schema.json` and a `phax.user.schema.json` that describe the `brief` key, leaving `phax.json` unchanged.

requirements.title: The pushed brief, once per fresh phase start
requirements.statement: WHEN a phase starts fresh with a brief provider configured, whether on its first run, on a re-run after `phax reset-phase`, or when appended by `phax run --append`, THE system SHALL request the pushed brief once, after the phase worktree is ready and before building the phase's first prompt.

requirements.title: No new pushed brief on resume
requirements.statement: WHEN a phase is resumed THE system SHALL NOT request the pushed brief again.

requirements.title: The phase facts are the gate request's
requirements.statement: WHILE a brief is requested for a phase THE system SHALL put the phase facts in the request, with exactly the values that the gate request of that phase carries.

requirements.title: The phase's brief has `files: null`
requirements.statement: WHEN the pushed brief is requested, or `phax brief` runs inside a phase with no path, THE system SHALL send the phase's brief request with `files` set to `null`.

requirements.title: Named paths, existing or not
requirements.statement: WHEN `phax brief` runs with one or more paths THE system SHALL set `files` to those paths, resolved against the current directory and made relative to the working tree root, in the order given and without duplicates, sending a path that does not exist exactly as it sends one that does.

requirements.title: Outside a phase, no phase facts
requirements.statement: WHEN `phax brief` runs with paths outside a phase THE system SHALL send a request holding only `$schema` and `files`.

requirements.title: Bad arguments
requirements.statement: IF `phax brief` runs outside a phase with no path, outside any git working tree, or with a path that resolves outside the working tree root THEN the system SHALL refuse the call with exit 1 and a message naming the problem, without running the provider.

requirements.title: Facts, never a judgement
requirements.statement: The system shall put no key in a brief request other than `$schema`, the phase facts and `files`: no state, rank, filter, touched files, diff or judgement.

requirements.title: The phase request file
requirements.statement: WHEN a phase starts or resumes with a brief provider configured THE system SHALL write the phase request file into the phase worktree before the agent's turn.

requirements.title: `phax brief` learns its phase from the file
requirements.statement: WHEN `phax brief` runs from any directory of a worktree THE system SHALL take the phase facts from that worktree's phase request file, and SHALL treat the call as outside a phase when the worktree has none.

requirements.title: An unreadable phase request file
requirements.statement: IF the phase request file exists but does not decode as a brief request THEN `phax brief` SHALL exit 1 with a message naming the file, without running the provider.

requirements.title: The brief answer's shape
requirements.statement: The system shall accept as a brief answer only a document `{ "$schema": …, "guarantees": [...] }` whose guarantees are `{id, statement, places}` with at least one place, and whose places are, by state, `met` `{location, state}`, `missing` or `forbidden` `{location, state, due, what, repair}`, or `accepted` `{location, state, what}`, ignoring any key beyond these.

requirements.title: The answer names its format and release
requirements.statement: The system shall require a brief answer's `$schema` to be `https://docs.phax.run/schemas/brief-answer/<release>.json`, and shall decode the answer with the shape of the latest `brief-answer` release at or below `<release>`.

requirements.title: A newer answer is refused by name
requirements.statement: IF a brief answer's `$schema` names a `brief-answer` release newer than the running phax THEN the system SHALL treat the brief as failed, with a reason naming `brief-answer` and that release.

requirements.title: No `$schema`, no fallback
requirements.statement: IF a brief answer has no `$schema`, or its `$schema` names another format, a malformed URL or a release with no known `brief-answer` shape, THEN the system SHALL treat the brief as failed with a reason naming `$schema`, trying no other decoding.

requirements.title: The provider's order is the rank
requirements.statement: The system shall render and record guarantees and places in the provider's order, never sorting, grouping, filtering or deduplicating them.

requirements.title: The compact form in the first prompt
requirements.statement: WHEN the pushed brief is answered THE system SHALL weave its compact form into a `## Brief for this phase` section of the phase's first prompt.

requirements.title: A cap of 50 guarantees on the pushed form
requirements.statement: IF the pushed brief holds more than 50 guarantees THEN the system SHALL weave the first 50 and one line that gives the number not shown and names `phax brief`.

requirements.title: The whole form on demand
requirements.statement: WHEN `phax brief` receives an answer THE system SHALL print the answer's whole form to stdout and exit 0.

requirements.title: Nothing to report
requirements.statement: WHEN an answer holds no guarantee THE system SHALL say that the provider has nothing to report, in the brief section for the pushed brief and on stdout with exit 0 for a pulled brief.

requirements.title: The brief time limit
requirements.statement: WHEN the brief provider has not exited within the brief time limit THE system SHALL stop it and treat the brief as failed.

requirements.title: A failed pushed brief does not stop the phase
requirements.statement: IF the pushed brief fails (the provider exits non-zero, prints no answer that decodes, or exceeds the brief time limit) THEN the system SHALL warn in the run output naming the phase and the reason, weave the brief section with a line saying the brief is unavailable and why, and run the phase.

requirements.title: A failed pulled brief is reported
requirements.statement: IF a pulled brief fails THEN `phax brief` SHALL print the reason on stderr and exit 1.

requirements.title: A brief changes no verdict
requirements.statement: The system shall let no brief, brief answer or brief failure change a gate verdict, the fix loop, a phase or run state, or the exit code of `phax run` or `phax resume`.

requirements.title: `phax brief` is granted to the in-phase agent
requirements.statement: WHERE a brief provider is configured THE system SHALL allow `phax brief` to the in-phase agent without an `agentCommands` entry, recording the grant in `security.json` with source `brief`.

requirements.title: No provider, no brief in the phase
requirements.statement: WHERE no brief provider is configured THE system SHALL weave no brief section, write no phase request file and no brief record, and grant no `phax brief`.

requirements.title: No provider, `phax brief` says so
requirements.statement: IF `phax brief` runs with no brief provider configured THEN the system SHALL exit 1 with a message naming the `brief` key.

requirements.title: What the agent is told
requirements.statement: WHERE a brief provider is configured THE system SHALL end the brief section with three instructions: to run `phax brief <path>…` before touching any file, planned or not and existing or not; to run `phax brief` with no path for the phase's brief in whole form; and to run the gate commands listed in the prompt to learn where the phase stands.

requirements.title: The pushed brief is recorded
requirements.statement: WHEN the pushed brief is answered or fails THE system SHALL save `brief-00.json` in the phase folder, holding `moment: "pushed"`, the request exactly as sent and the outcome.

requirements.title: Each pulled brief is recorded
requirements.statement: WHEN `phax brief` runs inside a phase whose record is not yet written THE system SHALL add to that phase's folder a brief record holding `moment: "pulled"`, the request exactly as sent and the outcome, numbered from `01` in call order across all of the phase's sessions.

requirements.title: The answer is recorded as printed
requirements.statement: The system shall hold an answered brief's answer in its brief record as the JSON value the provider printed, its `$schema` and any extra key included, never re-stamped or re-shaped.

requirements.title: What is not recorded
requirements.statement: The system shall record nothing for a `phax brief` call made outside a phase or after the phase's record is written.

requirements.title: Three persisted formats
requirements.statement: The system shall define `brief-request`, `brief-answer` and `brief-record` as persisted formats in `@lbdremy/phax-schemas`. Each has `$schema` `https://docs.phax.run/schemas/<format>/<release>.json`, a parser (`parseBriefRequest`, `parseBriefAnswer`, `parseBriefRecord`), recognition by `parseDocument`, and a JSON Schema under `json/`.

requirements.title: `records explain` shows the briefs
requirements.statement: WHEN `phax records explain <commit> --briefs` runs on a phase record THE system SHALL print each of the phase's brief records in number order, each under its file name.

requirements.title: The docs describe the brief
requirements.statement: The system's README (§Extend phax and §Persisted formats), `phax --usage`, CLI reference and generated config schemas shall describe the brief provider, its request and versioned answer, and `phax brief`.

requirements.title: The hello-world example has a brief provider
requirements.statement: The hello-world example shall declare a `brief` provider. It is backed by a small static script that answers both the phase's brief and named paths with a `$schema`-carrying answer, and the example-provider tests exercise it.

The audit and the gate: the gate request, the versioned diagnostics document, verdicts, fix prompts and attribution belong to `gate-request` and `drop-gate-scopes`, and nothing in them changes here.

openQuestions.question: What shape does the brief answer take? (Decided by the author on 2026-10-05; not reopened.)

options.label: Structured: guarantees → places with a per-state variant; phax renders the compact and whole forms and records the data
options.abandons: The provider's control over wording and layout. A field set is frozen before 1.0 for a provider that is not built yet.

options.label: Text the provider renders: `{compact, whole}` strings that phax weaves and prints verbatim
options.abandons: The brief as data. Records would hold prose no tool can read back, phax could not cap the pushed form by guarantee or check the states, and the provider would maintain two renderings.

options.label: Both: the structured answer plus provider-rendered text
options.abandons: One account of the answer. The two renderings can disagree, and both become contract.

openQuestions.rationale: Decided by the author on 2026-10-05, as recommended. One structured answer serves both moments: phax cuts the compact form from it and prints the whole form, so the provider answers once. steme's ledger is structured already, and the states are exactly what the agent needs to read. The frozen field set is the acceptable loss because it is kept to what the first consumer needs (id, statement, location, state, due, what, repair), and extra keys pass decoding, so steme can add fields before phax reads them.

openQuestions.question: How does `phax brief`, run by the agent inside the phase worktree, learn the phase it is in? (Decided by the author on 2026-10-05; not reopened.)

options.label: A file phax writes into the worktree: `.phax-context/brief-request.json`, the phase's brief request with `files: null`
options.abandons: Tamper-proof facts. `.phax-context/` is writable by the agent, which could edit or delete the file and so mislead its own brief, though never a verdict.

options.label: An environment variable in the agent's session (run and phase ids)
options.abandons: Provider neutrality. Whether a variable reaches the commands an agent runs is up to each provider CLI (Codex filters its shell environment by policy), and every resumed session must be launched with it.

options.label: Flags on the command: `phax brief --run <id> --phase <id> [paths]`
options.abandons: An agent that never handles plumbing. Every call repeats ids phax already knows, and a wrong id sends another phase's facts.

options.label: None: `phax brief` always briefs as the code stands
options.abandons: The phase facts on every pull. A pulled brief could not say what is due this phase, which is half the need.

openQuestions.rationale: Decided by the author on 2026-10-05, as recommended. The file works the same under every provider and under a sandbox that confines the agent to its worktree. It survives a resume because phax rewrites it. It holds the facts themselves, so `phax brief` never has to reach into the run state, and a person can replay it with `steme brief < .phax-context/brief-request.json`. The tampering risk is the acceptable loss: an edited file can only mislead the agent's own advice, and the audit reads its facts from phax, not from the worktree.

openQuestions.question: Is the brief's request the gate request's format, or its own? (Decided by the author on 2026-10-05; not reopened.)

options.label: Its own format `brief-request`: the gate request's four fact keys with the same names, types and values, plus `files`; outside a phase, `$schema` and `files` only
options.abandons: A single parser for both verbs. A provider reads two formats, one being the other plus `files`.

options.label: The gate request extended with `files` (null for the gate)
options.abandons: gate-request's settled "exactly five keys", and a gate step would receive a key that means nothing to it. It also leaves no shape for a call outside a phase.

options.label: The gate request verbatim on stdin, with the paths as arguments to the provider command
options.abandons: Stdin as the single channel. Paths become argv that the provider must parse, and outside a phase there is no gate request to send.

openQuestions.rationale: Decided by the author on 2026-10-05, as recommended. The facts are shared by value, not by format: for the same phase, `phase`, `base`, `terminal` and `phases` are identical in both documents, which is what keeps the two verbs from disagreeing. The approved gate request stays untouched. The out-of-phase call gets an explicit variant instead of null facts, and `$schema` tells a provider which verb it is serving. A second, nearly identical parser is a small price.

openQuestions.question: Does the pushed form keep a cap, and which? (Decided by the author on 2026-10-05; not reopened.)

options.label: Keep a cap of 50 guarantees, in provider order, with a not-shown line naming `phax brief`
options.abandons: The provider's whole word in the prompt. Guarantees past the 50th reach the agent only if it pulls, whether or not they are due this phase.

options.label: No cap
options.abandons: A bound on every phase prompt. A provider answering with thousands of guarantees inflates the cost of each first prompt.

options.label: A cap in bytes or lines
options.abandons: A cut the agent can reason about. Where the text stops depends on statement lengths, not on rank, and the cut can fall mid-guarantee.

openQuestions.rationale: Decided by the author on 2026-10-05, as recommended. Order is the provider's rank, so the cut drops what the provider ranks lowest, and the not-shown line says how to reach the rest. Counting guarantees keeps each one whole. 50 was orient's cap and caused no trouble. Losing the tail from the prompt is acceptable because the tail is one `phax brief` away, and a provider that ranks due guarantees first loses nothing that matters.

openQuestions.question: Can a guarantee be asked for by id (`phax brief <id> [paths]`)? (Decided by the author on 2026-10-05; not reopened.)

options.label: No: `phax brief [path…]` only
options.abandons: Re-reading one guarantee without the others on the same paths. The agent finds it in the whole answer instead.

options.label: Yes: `phax brief <id> [paths]`, with the request gaining a `guarantee` key
options.abandons: One argument grammar: an id and a path are both bare words, and `money-as-cents` could be a file. It also adds a request key and a provider behaviour the first consumer does not need.

openQuestions.rationale: Decided by the author on 2026-10-05, as recommended. orient needed expand because its index carried no body. A whole brief already carries every statement, state, `what` and repair, so the agent never needs a second round trip. Keeping to what the first consumer needs, the lost convenience is small and can be added later as a new key without breaking the request.

openQuestions.question: Does severity survive once state is in the answer? (Decided by the author on 2026-10-05; not reopened.)

options.label: Drop severity
options.abandons: A per-guarantee weight independent of order. A provider can no longer say error versus info.

options.label: Keep `severity: error|warn|info` per guarantee, beside state
options.abandons: One ranking signal. Severity and order can disagree, and phax would render a second rank that it did not make and cannot reconcile.

openQuestions.rationale: Decided by the author on 2026-10-05, as recommended. State says what to do at a place (fix what is missing or forbidden, leave accepted debt alone), and due says when; order says what matters most. Severity added a third axis that only made sense when the answer carried no state, and the audit, not the brief, is where weight becomes a verdict. Losing the explicit label is acceptable because the provider still ranks by order.

openQuestions.question: What happens to a `phax brief` call made in a phase worktree after that phase's record is written (the kept-open final phase in review)? (Decided by the author on 2026-10-06; not reopened.)

options.label: Answer it with the phase's facts and record nothing
options.abandons: A complete account of what was asked during review. Pulls made while the final phase is kept open leave no trace in the record.

options.label: Record it into the already-written record, or a follow-up record
options.abandons: A phase record written once. `phax/records/v1` would need an amendment path it does not have, for calls that no longer shape the phase's gated work.

options.label: Refuse the call once the record is written
options.abandons: The brief during review, when a person or a review session still edits files in that worktree and needs the same advice.

openQuestions.rationale: Decided by the author on 2026-10-06, as recommended. The record explains the gated phase, and every brief that shaped that work was made before the record was written, so it is captured. Review-time pulls inform edits that the review itself accounts for. Losing their trace is the cheapest of the three losses: amending records changes a persisted contract, and refusing removes the advice when it is still useful.

openQuestions.question: What does `phax brief` do when the phase request file is present but does not decode? (Decided by the author on 2026-10-06; not reopened.)

options.label: Exit 1 naming the file, without running the provider
options.abandons: An answer while the file is damaged. The agent must restore it (a resume rewrites it), or delete it to brief as outside a phase.

options.label: Brief as outside a phase
options.abandons: Noticing the damage. Every pull silently loses the phase facts and `due`, and nothing says why.

openQuestions.rationale: Decided by the author on 2026-10-06, as recommended. A present file means the call is inside a phase. Silently falling back would hand the agent advice without the half of the need that depends on the phase (what is due now). A loud refusal costs one call and names the file to fix.

openQuestions.question: Is the brief time limit fixed or configurable, and how long is it? (Decided by the author on 2026-10-06; not reopened.)

options.label: A fixed 60 seconds, the same for pushed and pulled briefs
options.abandons: A provider that needs longer on a large repository. It is cut off, and the phase runs without its brief, or the pull fails.

options.label: A `timeoutSeconds` beside `command` in the `brief` key
options.abandons: The `{command}`-only shape every provider key shares, and one more config key frozen at 1.0 before the first consumer has shown it needs one.

options.label: No limit
options.abandons: Never blocking. A wedged provider wedges the phase start, as orient's unbounded query could.

openQuestions.rationale: Decided by the author on 2026-10-06, as recommended. A brief reads a ledger the audit has already built, so it should answer in seconds. A fixed limit keeps every provider key `{command}` and keeps the config contract small before the freeze. If a real provider is too slow, the cost is a brief marked unavailable, never a blocked phase, and a key can be added later without breaking any existing config.

openQuestions.question: Does the brief answer carry its own `$schema`, and what does phax do with an answer that has none or names a newer release? (Decided by the author on 2026-10-06; not reopened.)

options.label: Required `$schema` naming the `brief-answer` format and release. phax decodes every supported release by its own shape and refuses a newer one by name. An answer with no `$schema` is a failed brief, with no fallback. The record holds the answer as printed.
options.abandons: A provider that prints a bare `{guarantees}`. Every provider must stamp the release it writes for, and an unstamped answer is reported as a failed brief instead of being read.

options.label: No `$schema` on the answer: its shape is implied by the request's `$schema`
options.abandons: Several answer versions at once. A provider can only answer in the shape of the release that asked, and a shape change silently misreads every older provider instead of naming the mismatch.

options.label: `$schema` optional, a missing one read as the current release's shape
options.abandons: A hard contract at the boundary. It is a back-compat shim in a persisted format born with `$schema`, and a mis-stamped or unstamped answer is decoded by guesswork rather than refused.

openQuestions.rationale: Decided by the author on 2026-10-06, as recommended: every JSON document that crosses a provider boundary is versioned in both directions, as the gate request and the diagnostics document already are. With the release in the answer, phax can keep reading an older provider's answers through the schemas package's history mechanism while the shape evolves, and it names the release it cannot read instead of failing on a field. Recording the answer as printed keeps the provider's own `$schema` in the record, so a reader decodes it by the shape it was written in. Losing the bare answer costs a provider one key, and no provider exists yet (steme's `brief` is not built). An unstamped answer is reported and never blocks, so the strict rule costs no phase.

settled: Config: `brief: {command}` in the three layers, read from phax.local.json, then ~/.phax/config.json, then phax.json, like `planAuditor`. `phax schema upgrade` regenerates both local schemas and never touches `phax.json`. Nothing about `orient` appears: since `drop-orient` it is an unknown key like any other.

Request: its own format, `brief-request`. Inside a phase it holds `$schema`, the phase facts (the same values as the phase's gate request) and `files`. `files` is `null` for the phase's brief. Otherwise it holds the named paths: relative to the working tree root, deduplicated, in the order given, and never checked for existence. Outside a phase the request holds `$schema` and `files` only. The provider runs from the working tree root.

Phase identity: the phase request file `.phax-context/brief-request.json`, written at phase start and on resume when `brief` is configured. `phax brief` reads it from any directory of the worktree. With no file the call is outside a phase. A file that does not decode is refused (Q8).

Answer: its own format, `brief-answer`, `{$schema, guarantees: [{id, statement, places}]}`. Each guarantee has at least one place, and places have per-state variants. `due` sits on `missing` and `forbidden` places. `location` is `{file, line?}`, as in a diagnostics finding. Extra keys are ignored. The provider's order is the rank. There is no severity, title, trigger or body.

Answer versioning (Q10): `$schema` is required and names `brief-answer` and a release. phax decodes it with the latest shape at or below that release, through the schemas package's history mechanism, as for every persisted format. A newer release fails with a reason naming `brief-answer` and the release. A missing `$schema`, another format, a malformed URL or an unknown release fails at `$schema`. Each failure is an ordinary failed brief: it never blocks and has no fallback. The format is born with `$schema`, so it has no pre-schema shape.

Pushed brief: requested once per fresh phase start (first run, after reset-phase, appended), after the worktree is ready and before the first prompt. It is not requested on resume, and it does not appear in fix-loop, review or compliance prompts. It is woven in compact form under `## Brief for this phase`, capped at 50 guarantees with a not-shown line, and followed by the three instructions. With `files: null`, the provider briefs the gated phase's entry in `phases` (create ∪ edit, optional files excluded). The agent pulls an optional file when it decides to touch it.

Pulled brief: `phax brief [path…]` prints the whole form. It exits 0 on any answer and 1 otherwise: failure, refused answer, missing provider, unreadable phase request file, or bad arguments. README §Exit codes files bad arguments under 1 and reserves 2 for plan or config validation. There is no lookup by id.

Never blocks: every call has the fixed brief time limit (Q9: 60 seconds). A failure produces a run-output warning, an unavailable line in the prompt and a `failed` record. It never affects a verdict, a state, or the exit code of `phax run` or `phax resume`.

Records: `brief-NN.json` (format `brief-record`). `00` is the pushed brief, and `01`… are the pulled ones in call order across sessions. An answered outcome holds the answer as printed, with its own `$schema` and any extra key, never re-stamped. Records go into the phase record and print with `phax records explain --briefs`. Nothing is recorded outside a phase or after the phase's record is written (Q7).

Formats: `brief-request`, `brief-answer` and `brief-record` in `@lbdremy/phax-schemas`. Each has a parser, `parseDocument` recognition, a JSON Schema under `json/`, a README §Persisted formats row and a `next` snapshot until released.
Grant: `phax brief` is allowed automatically when `brief` is configured, and `security.json` gains the source value `brief` (phax-internal, not a package format).
open: How a pulled call's record reaches the phase folder. `phax brief` runs as a child of the agent, and the sandbox may confine it to the worktree. The likely route is to write under `.phax-context/` and collect the files into the phase folder before the record is written.

How `base` is available before the agent's first turn. The pushed brief needs it at phase start, and spec `gate-request` notes it when the phase branch is created. Read it the same way, so the two documents cannot differ.

Whether a pulled brief's provider, run inside the agent's sandbox, can read what it needs (for steme, its ledger). If the ledger lives outside the worktree, the sandbox posture for `phax brief` must allow it. Raise this with the steme item 8 design.
How `brief-record`'s JSON Schema embeds the answer: by reference to `brief-answer` across its releases, or as an open object whose `$schema` the parser resolves.
The exact compact line, the whole-form layout, the section heading and position, the instruction wording and the refusal wording (indicative in §6).
Whether `phax records explain` without flags mentions the briefs. A one-line count is suggested.
Whether briefs emit telemetry events (the observability port) in addition to the records. This spec does not require them.

The steme-corpus coordination note (`02-product/phax-steme-coordination.md`: §Along a run, §What is lost, or latent, §The changes rows 4 and 5, §The architecture brief, at plan authoring) could not be read from this authoring session. The re-authored `drop-gate-scopes` spec was not yet under docs/specs/, so it was read from its brief. The planner should cross-check both. This spec supersedes rows 4 and 5 of the note.
constraints: A brief never blocks, and phax judges nothing in it. phax ranks, filters and deduplicates nothing, computes no state or due, and does not cross-check the answer against the request. Decoding the answer by its `$schema` is the only check.
Lands after `drop-orient`, `drop-gate-scopes` and `gate-request`. The phase facts are the gate request's, with the same values for the same phase.
Purely additive: one key, one command, one prompt section, one `records explain` flag, one grant source value and three persisted formats. Nothing is retired, aliased or migrated.
No back-compat shim: `brief-answer` is born with a required `$schema`, and no unstamped shape is ever read.
phax ties the `brief` provider to no gate step. `steme brief` and `steme audit` are configured separately and share only the facts phax sends.
This spec lands before steme builds item 8 (`steme brief`). Keep the answer to the fields named here, so the first consumer is not frozen into more.
Relation to oracle-phases (Approved, not built; its text is unchanged): its `oracles: {command}` key sits beside `brief` and `planAuditor` with the same shape.
This changes the CLI and config surface on purpose before the 1.0 freeze.

docsPage.page: README §Extend phax › Brief provider, with the `brief-request`, `brief-answer` and `brief-record` rows in §Persisted formats and `phax brief` in docs/cli/reference.md
docsPage.reader: The author of a brief provider, such as steme's `steme brief`. They need to know what phax sends at phase start and on each pull, what versioned answer it expects, and that phax never judges the answer. A secondary reader is the operator who wants to see what the agent was told during a run.
docsPage.example: Declare `"brief": { "command": "node ./brief.mjs" }`. In brief.mjs, read stdin to the end and parse it. When `files` is null, brief the files of the `phases` entry whose `id` is `phase`. Otherwise brief `files`, which may include paths that do not exist yet. When `phase` is present, set `due` to `this-phase` or `later` from what later entries of `phases` still plan. Outside a phase, set `due` to null. Print `{ "$schema": "https://docs.phax.run/schemas/brief-answer/0.20.0.json", "guarantees": [{ "id": "hw-no-io", "statement": "greet has no I/O", "places": [{ "location": { "file": "src/greet.ts", "line": 1 }, "state": "forbidden", "due": "this-phase", "what": "imports node:fs", "repair": "remove the import; greet is pure" }] }] }`, most important first. `$schema` names the phax release whose answer shape you wrote. A later phax keeps reading it, and an older phax refuses it by name. Replay a phase's brief with `node ./brief.mjs < .phax-context/brief-request.json`, and a recorded one with `jq -c .request brief-01.json | node ./brief.mjs`.
